about: House recipes, batch 04 (helper sA): written by Claude in a Max-plan session, original, ai-draft. Nutrition is a per-serve estimate kept as data only.

recipes.title: Sheikh al Mahshi (Lebanese Lamb-Stuffed Zucchini in Yoghurt)
recipes.summary: Small zucchini filled with spiced lamb and pine nuts, simmered in a tangy warm yoghurt sauce.
steps: Hollow out the zucchini with a corer, leaving the walls about 5mm thick.
Cook the onion in the oil over medium heat for 5 minutes, until soft. Add the lamb, allspice, salt and pepper and cook for 8 minutes, until browned. Stir in the rice and pine nuts.
Fill each zucchini about three quarters full and arrange in a wide pot.

Whisk the yoghurt, egg white and cornflour in a saucepan over low heat, stirring in one direction, until it just starts to bubble. Pour over the zucchini, add the garlic and 1/2 cup water and simmer gently for 25 minutes, until the zucchini are tender.
Scatter the mint over and serve with the sauce spooned around.
notes: Food safety: mince must reach 75°C in the centre with no pink inside. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot.
Always stir the yoghurt in one direction over low heat so it does not split.

recipes.title: Fatteh bil Djej (Levantine Chicken Fatteh)
recipes.summary: Layers of crisp pita, chickpeas and shredded chicken under garlicky yoghurt and toasted pine nuts.
steps: Put the chicken, onion and cinnamon in a pot, cover with water and simmer for 25 minutes, until cooked through. Lift out the chicken and shred it. Keep 1/2 cup of the stock.
Tear the pita into pieces, toss with the oil and bake at 200°C (180°C fan) for 8 minutes, until crisp.
Warm the chickpeas in the reserved stock for 3 minutes. Whisk the yoghurt, garlic, tahini and lemon juice with salt.
Toast the pine nuts in the butter for 2 minutes, until golden.
Layer the pita in a deep dish, add the chickpeas with a little stock, then the chicken and yoghurt. Top with the pine nuts and parsley and serve straight away.
notes: Food safety: chicken must reach 75°C in the thickest part with no pink juices. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot.
Assemble at the last minute so the pita keeps some crunch.

recipes.title: Chicken Mandi (Yemeni Spiced Rice with Chicken)
recipes.summary: Fragrant long grain rice with tender spiced chicken, a Yemeni feast dish cooked until the meat falls off the bone.
steps: Rub the chicken with the oil, half the spices, the garlic and 1 tsp salt. Rest at room temperature while you start the rice, up to 30 minutes.
Brown the chicken in a large heavy pot over medium-high heat for 8 minutes. Add the onion and tomato and cook for 5 minutes.
Add the stock and bring to a simmer. Cover and cook for 30 minutes, until the chicken is very tender. Lift out the chicken.
Rinse the rice until the water runs clear. Add the rice and remaining spices to the stock, cover and cook on low for 15 minutes, until the stock is absorbed.
Meanwhile, grill the chicken for 6 minutes, until the skin is crisp. Fry the almonds and sultanas in the butter for 2 minutes. Pile the rice on a platter, top with the chicken, almonds and sultanas.
notes: Food safety: chicken must reach 75°C in the thickest part with no pink juices. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot.
Cool leftover rice quickly and eat within a day.

recipes.title: Saltah (Yemeni Lamb and Vegetable Stew)
recipes.summary: A bubbling Yemeni stew of lamb, tomato and lentils, served in a hot dish with rice.
steps: Brown the lamb in the oil in a heavy pot over high heat for 8 minutes, until deeply coloured. Add the onion and garlic and cook for 4 minutes.
Stir in the tomato paste, tomato and spices and cook for 3 minutes, until thick.
Add the water, lentils and 1 tsp salt. Cover and simmer for 45 minutes, until the lamb is tender.
Add the potato and capsicum and cook for 15 minutes, until the potato is soft and the stew is thick.
Serve in bowls over the rice, with extra black pepper and a squeeze of lemon if you like.
notes: Food safety: lamb pieces should reach at least 70°C and be tender. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour; reheat until steaming hot.
Dairy-free and gluten-free.

recipes.title: Ghormeh Sabzi (Persian Herb and Lamb Stew)
recipes.summary: The classic Persian herb stew with lamb, kidney beans and dried lime, deep green and sour.
steps: Brown the lamb with the onion and turmeric in half the oil in a heavy pot for 10 minutes.
Fry the herbs in the remaining oil in a pan over medium heat for 10 minutes, until dark and fragrant.
Add the herbs, pierced dried limes and water to the lamb. Cover and simmer on low for 1 1/2 hours, until the lamb is very tender.
Add the beans and simmer for 20 minutes. Season, then add lemon juice to taste.
Spoon the stew over the rice in shallow bowls and serve hot.
notes: Food safety: lamb pieces should reach at least 70°C and be tender. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour; reheat until steaming hot.
Canned beans are already cooked. If you use dried kidney beans, soak them overnight and boil hard for 10 minutes before they go in.
Dairy-free and gluten-free. Better the next day.

recipes.title: Fesenjan (Persian Chicken in Walnut and Pomegranate Sauce)
recipes.summary: Chicken braised in a rich, sweet-sour sauce of ground walnuts and pomegranate molasses.
steps: Toast the walnuts in a dry pan for 5 minutes, then grind finely in a food processor.
Cook the onion in the oil in a heavy pot over medium heat for 10 minutes, until golden. Add the turmeric and the chicken and brown for 5 minutes.
Add the walnuts and water and bring to a simmer. Cover and cook on low for 40 minutes, stirring now and then.
Stir in the molasses, honey and cinnamon and cook uncovered for 20 minutes, until the sauce is thick and dark. Taste and balance the sweet and sour.
Spoon the chicken and sauce over the rice on warm plates and serve at once.
notes: Food safety: chicken must reach 75°C in the thickest part with no pink juices. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot.
Contains walnuts. Dairy-free and gluten-free.

recipes.title: Zereshk Polo ba Morgh (Persian Rice with Saffron Chicken)
recipes.summary: Buttery saffron rice jewelled with sweet sultanas, served with tender saffron chicken.
steps: Grind the saffron with a pinch of salt and steep in 3 tbsp hot water.
Brown the onion in the oil for 8 minutes. Add the chicken, half the saffron, tomatoes and 1 cup water. Cover and simmer for 35 minutes, until tender.
Boil the rice in plenty of salted water for 6 minutes, until just soft outside and firm inside. Drain.
Fry the sultanas (or barberries, if you can find them) in 1 tbsp butter with the sugar for 1 minute, until plump.

Layer the rice in the pot with the remaining butter, the rest of the saffron water and a tea towel under the lid. Steam on low for 25 minutes. Pile onto a platter, scatter the sultanas and almonds over and serve with the chicken.
notes: Food safety: chicken must reach 75°C in the thickest part with no pink juices. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot.
Gluten-free.

recipes.title: Joojeh Kabab (Persian Saffron Chicken Skewers)
recipes.summary: Juicy saffron and yoghurt marinated chicken pieces grilled over high heat.

items: 800g chicken thigh fillets, cut into chunks

steps: Steep the saffron in 2 tbsp hot water. Mix with the onion (and its juice), yoghurt, lemon juice, oil, garlic, salt and pepper. Add the chicken and marinate in the fridge for at least 4 hours.
Thread onto flat skewers with the tomatoes at the ends.
Grill over a hot barbecue or griddle for 10 to 12 minutes, turning, until browned at the edges and cooked through.
Slide the chicken off the skewers onto a bed of rice with the grilled tomatoes and spoon over any juices from the platter.
notes: Food safety: chicken must reach 75°C in the thickest part with no pink juices. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot.
Marinate in the fridge, never on the bench. Discard leftover marinade.

recipes.title: Kubideh (Persian Minced Lamb Kebabs)
recipes.summary: Soft, onion-rich minced lamb kebabs pressed on to flat skewers and grilled.
steps: Squeeze the onion dry. Knead it with the mince, turmeric, salt and pepper for 5 minutes, until sticky and well combined.
With wet hands, mould the mince around flat skewers in a long sausage shape, pressing flat with finger dents.
Grill the kebabs and tomatoes on a hot barbecue or griddle for 8 to 10 minutes, turning once, until cooked through.
Brush with butter, dust with sumac and serve in the flatbread.
notes: Food safety: mince must reach 75°C in the centre with no pink inside. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot.
Chill the shaped skewers for 30 minutes so they hold together.

recipes.title: Adana Kebab (Turkish Spicy Lamb Kebabs)
recipes.summary: Hand-chopped style lamb kebabs with tail-fat richness and chilli, grilled on wide skewers.
steps: Squeeze out the capsicum and onion well, then knead into the lamb with the pepper, cumin and salt for 5 minutes.
Press around wide skewers in a long flat shape. Chill for 30 minutes.
Toss the sliced onion, parsley and sumac with the oil.
Grill over high heat for 8 to 10 minutes, turning, until browned and cooked through. Serve in flatbread with the onion.
notes: Food safety: mince must reach 75°C in the centre with no pink inside. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot.
Use less Aleppo pepper if you like it mild.

recipes.title: Iskender Kebab (Turkish Sliced Lamb on Pide with Tomato and Yoghurt)
recipes.summary: Thin lamb strips over torn pide, with hot tomato sauce, melted butter and cool yoghurt.
steps: Season the lamb with the cumin, oregano, salt and pepper. Sear in batches in the oil over high heat for 2 minutes per side, until browned and cooked through.
Cook the onion and garlic in the same pan for 4 minutes. Add the paste and tomatoes and simmer for 15 minutes, until thick.
Toast the pide until crisp at the edges, then tear into pieces. Divide among plates.
Top with the lamb and tomato sauce. Melt the butter until it sizzles and pour it over, then spoon on the yoghurt.
notes: Food safety: lamb slices should reach at least 70°C with no pink. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour.
Serve straight away so the bread stays soft rather than soggy.

recipes.title: Manti (Turkish Lamb Dumplings with Garlic Yoghurt)
recipes.summary: Tiny lamb dumplings baked until crisp, served with garlic yoghurt and chilli butter.
steps: Knead the flour, egg, water and 1/2 tsp salt into a firm dough. Rest for 30 minutes.
Mix the lamb with the onion, parsley, salt and pepper.
Roll the dough very thin, cut into 3cm squares and place a pinch of filling in each. Pinch the corners together to seal.
Bake the manti in a 220°C (200°C fan) tray for 15 minutes, until golden. Pour over the hot stock and bake for 10 minutes more.
Mix the yoghurt and garlic. Melt the butter with the paprika and mint. Serve the manti with the yoghurt and the spiced butter.
notes: Food safety: mince must reach 75°C in the centre with no pink inside. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot.
Freeze uncooked manti on a tray, then bag them. Cook from frozen, adding 5 minutes.

recipes.title: Karniyarik (Turkish Eggplant Stuffed with Spiced Lamb)
recipes.summary: Split eggplants fried until soft and filled with a tomato and lamb mixture, baked until sticky.
steps: Peel the eggplants in stripes and slit lengthways, leaving the ends joined. Salt lightly and rest for 15 minutes, then pat dry.
Fry the eggplants in the oil over medium heat for 10 minutes, turning, until soft and golden. Place in a baking dish.
Cook the onion and garlic in a little oil, add the lamb and cook for 8 minutes. Add the tomato, capsicum, half the paste and the parsley and cook for 6 minutes.
Open the eggplants and pack in the filling. Mix the rest of the paste with the water and pour around.
Cover and bake at 190°C (170°C fan) for 30 minutes, until tender.
notes: Food safety: mince must reach 75°C in the centre with no pink inside. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot.
Dairy-free and gluten-free.

recipes.title: Hunkar Begendi (Turkish Lamb Stew on Smoky Eggplant Puree)
recipes.summary: The Sultan's Delight: tender lamb stew over a creamy, smoky eggplant and cheese puree.
steps: Brown the lamb in the oil for 8 minutes. Add the onion and cook for 4 minutes, then the tomato, capsicum, paste, water, salt and pepper. Cover and simmer for 1 hour, until tender.
Char the eggplants over a gas flame or under a hot grill for 15 minutes, turning, until blackened and collapsed. Peel and mash the flesh.
Melt the butter, whisk in the flour for 1 minute, then add the milk and cook until thick. Stir in the eggplant and cheese for 4 minutes, until smooth.
Spoon the puree on plates and top with the lamb.
notes: Food safety: lamb pieces should reach at least 70°C and be tender. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour.
Uses mild cheddar, which is not suitable for vegetarians.

recipes.title: Nashville Hot Chicken
recipes.summary: Crisp fried chicken brushed with a fiery cayenne oil and served on white bread with pickles.
steps: Soak the chicken in the buttermilk, hot sauce and 1 tsp salt in the fridge for at least 4 hours.
Mix the flour, smoked paprika, garlic powder and 1 tsp salt. Dredge the chicken, pressing the flour on.
Heat the oil to 170°C in a deep heavy pot. Fry in two batches for 14 minutes, until deep golden and 75°C inside. Drain on a rack.
Whisk 1/3 cup of the hot frying oil with the cayenne, sugar and paprika. Brush it over the chicken.
Serve on the bread with pickles.
notes: Food safety: chicken must reach 75°C in the thickest part with no pink juices. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot.
Hot oil can spit and ignite: never fill a pot more than a third full and keep a lid nearby. Wear gloves when handling the cayenne oil.

recipes.title: Southern Smothered Pork Chops
recipes.summary: Pan-fried chops simmered in a dark onion gravy until fork-tender.
steps: Season the chops with salt, pepper, paprika and garlic powder, then dust in 1/4 cup of the flour.
Brown in the oil in a large lidded pan over medium-high heat for 4 minutes per side. Lift out.
Cook the onion in the pan for 8 minutes, until golden. Stir in the garlic and the remaining flour for 1 minute. Add the stock, thyme and Worcestershire and stir until smooth.
Return the chops, cover and simmer gently for 25 minutes, until tender and the gravy has thickened.
Spoon the chops and onion gravy over the rice on warm plates and serve hot.
notes: Food safety: pork must reach at least 70°C in the centre and rest before serving. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour.
Dairy-free.

recipes.title: Shrimp Etouffee
recipes.summary: Prawns smothered in a roux-based Creole sauce with the holy trinity of onion, capsicum and celery.
steps: Melt the butter in a heavy pot and stir in the flour. Cook, stirring, for 8 minutes, until the roux is the colour of peanut butter.
Add the onion, capsicum and celery and cook for 8 minutes, until soft. Stir in the garlic, paste and seasoning for 1 minute.
Whisk in the stock, add the bay leaves and simmer for 15 minutes, until thick.
Add the prawns and cook for 4 minutes, until pink and opaque. Remove the bay leaves, add the spring onion and serve over rice.
notes: Food safety: prawns are cooked when pink and opaque all through; do not overcook or they turn rubbery. Eat the same day or refrigerate within an hour and use within 24 hours.
Contains shellfish. Cajun seasoning is salty, so taste before adding extra salt.

recipes.title: Chicken and Andouille Gumbo
recipes.summary: A deep brown roux gumbo with chicken thigh, smoked sausage and okra, served over rice.
steps: Whisk the oil and flour in a heavy pot over medium-low heat for 30 to 40 minutes, stirring constantly, until the roux is the colour of dark chocolate. Do not stop stirring or it will burn.
Add the onion, capsicum and celery and cook for 6 minutes. Add the garlic and cook for 1 minute.
Gradually whisk in the stock. Add the chicken, sausage, seasoning and bay leaves and simmer for 40 minutes.
Add the okra and cook for 10 minutes. Skim off excess oil, season and serve over rice.
notes: Food safety: chicken must reach 75°C in the thickest part with no pink juices. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot.
Roux is extremely hot and sticks to skin. Take care when adding the vegetables, as they will spit.

recipes.title: Shrimp Creole
recipes.summary: Prawns in a spicy tomato and capsicum sauce, served over steamed rice.
steps: Melt the butter in a large pan and cook the onion, capsicum and celery for 8 minutes, until soft. Add the garlic for 1 minute.
Add the tomatoes, stock, seasoning, paprika and bay leaves. Simmer for 15 minutes, until thick.
Add the prawns and cook for 4 minutes, until pink. Remove the bay leaves, stir in the hot sauce and serve over rice.
notes: Food safety: prawns are cooked when pink and opaque all through; do not overcook or they turn rubbery. Eat the same day or refrigerate within an hour and use within 24 hours.
Contains shellfish. Gluten-free.

recipes.title: King Ranch Chicken Casserole
recipes.summary: A Texas classic of shredded chicken, corn tortillas, cheese and a creamy chilli sauce baked until bubbling.
steps: Heat the oven to 190°C (170°C fan). Cook the onion and capsicum in the butter for 6 minutes. Stir in the flour, chilli and cumin for 1 minute, then whisk in the stock and cook until thick. Stir in the sour cream and tomatoes.
Tear the tortillas. Layer half in a baking dish, then half the chicken, half the sauce and a third of the cheese. Repeat, finishing with the remaining cheese.
Bake for 25 minutes, until golden and bubbling.
notes: Food safety: cook the chicken to 75°C before shredding and make sure the casserole is steaming hot in the middle. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour.
Uses cheddar, which is not suitable for vegetarians.

recipes.title: Loco Moco
recipes.summary: The Hawaiian comfort plate: a beef patty on rice, topped with a fried egg and rich brown gravy.
steps: Mix the mince, egg, breadcrumbs, garlic powder, salt and pepper and shape into 4 patties. Fry in the oil for 5 minutes per side, until cooked through. Rest.
Cook the onion in the butter for 8 minutes, until golden. Stir in the flour for 1 minute, then whisk in the stock and soy. Simmer for 6 minutes until thick.
Fry the 4 eggs sunny side up, or until the whites are fully set and the yolks as firm as you like.
Pile rice on plates, add a patty, an egg and the gravy.
notes: Food safety: mince must reach 75°C in the centre with no pink inside. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot. Cook the eggs until the whites are set; avoid runny yolks for the very young, elderly, pregnant or unwell.

recipes.title: Huli Huli Chicken
recipes.summary: Sweet, sticky grilled chicken with pineapple, soy and ginger, a Hawaiian roadside favourite.
steps: Mix the juice, soy, sugar, tomato sauce, ginger, garlic and vinegar. Reserve 1/2 cup and marinate the chicken in the rest in the fridge for at least 4 hours.
Heat the oven to 200°C (180°C fan). Bake the chicken for 30 minutes.
Simmer the reserved marinade for 5 minutes, until syrupy, and brush on the chicken. Grill for 8 minutes, turning, until charred in spots. Grill the pineapple for 2 minutes per side.
Serve with rice and the grilled pineapple, spooning any pan juices over.
notes: Food safety: chicken must reach 75°C in the thickest part with no pink juices. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot. Use only the reserved, unused marinade as a glaze.

recipes.title: Moqueca Baiana (Brazilian Fish and Coconut Stew)
recipes.summary: Fish simmered in coconut milk with tomato, capsicum and coriander, a Bahian favourite.

items: 600g firm white fish fillets, cut into chunks

steps: Toss the fish with the lime juice, 1 tsp salt and pepper. Marinate in the fridge for 20 minutes.
Cook the onion, capsicum and garlic in the oil in a wide pot for 8 minutes. Add the tomato and paprika for 4 minutes.
Pour in the coconut milk and simmer for 8 minutes. Add the fish and cook gently for 5 minutes, until opaque and flaking.
Stir in the coriander and serve with rice.
notes: Food safety: fish is cooked when opaque and reaches 63°C. Eat on the day or refrigerate within an hour and use within 24 hours.
Dairy-free and gluten-free.

recipes.title: Escondidinho de Carne (Brazilian Beef and Potato Mash Bake)
recipes.summary: Seasoned beef hidden under a golden layer of creamy mash and cheese.
steps: Boil the potato in salted water for 20 minutes, until very soft. Mash with the butter and milk until smooth.
Cook the onion in a pan for 5 minutes. Add the mince and cook for 8 minutes, until browned. Stir in the garlic, tomato, cumin and paste and cook for 8 minutes, until thick. Add the parsley.
Spread the beef in a baking dish and cover with the mash and mozzarella.
Bake at 200°C (180°C fan) for 20 minutes, until golden and bubbling.
notes: Food safety: mince must reach 75°C in the centre with no pink inside. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot.

recipes.title: Estrogonofe de Frango (Brazilian Chicken Stroganoff)
recipes.summary: Creamy chicken in a mild tomato and mushroom sauce, served with rice and crunchy potato sticks.
steps: Season the chicken and brown in the oil in a large pan for 6 minutes. Lift out.
Cook the onion and garlic for 4 minutes, add the mushroom and cook for 5 minutes.
Stir in the paste, tomato sauce and mustard, return the chicken and simmer for 8 minutes, until cooked through.
Stir in the cream and lime juice and warm through. Serve with rice and potato sticks.
notes: Food safety: chicken must reach 75°C in the thickest part with no pink juices. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot.
Do not boil after the cream goes in.

recipes.title: Milanesa Napolitana (Argentinian Crumbed Beef with Ham, Tomato and Cheese)
recipes.summary: A thin crumbed beef cutlet topped with napoli sauce, ham and melted cheese.
steps: Whisk the eggs with the garlic, parsley, salt and pepper. Dip the beef in the egg, then press into the breadcrumbs.
Shallow-fry in the oil for 3 minutes per side, until golden. Drain on paper.
Place on a tray, top with the passata, ham and cheese. Grill for 5 minutes, until melted and bubbling.
Serve the milanesas hot with a pile of chips and a wedge of lemon on the side.
notes: Food safety: beef must reach 75°C in the centre with no pink. Use separate hands and a clean plate for raw and cooked beef. Contains egg.
Flatten the beef thin between baking paper with a rolling pin if the butcher has not done it.

recipes.title: Pastel de Choclo (Chilean Corn and Beef Pie)
recipes.summary: A savoury pie of beef, olives and egg under a thick, golden crust of sweet corn.
steps: Cook the onion in the oil for 8 minutes. Add the beef and cook for 8 minutes, until browned. Stir in the cumin, paprika, salt and pepper. Spoon into a baking dish and top with the sultanas, olives and egg.
Blend the corn, basil, milk and butter into a thick puree. Cook in a pan, stirring, for 8 minutes, until it thickens.
Spread the corn over the filling and sprinkle with the sugar.
Bake at 200°C (180°C fan) for 25 minutes, until golden and browned in spots.
notes: Food safety: mince must reach 75°C in the centre with no pink inside. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot. Boil the eggs for 10 minutes and use within a day of cooking.
Contains egg.

recipes.title: Bandeja Paisa (Colombian Mixed Plate)
recipes.summary: The big Antioquian platter of beans, rice, pork, fried egg, plantain and avocado.

items: 1 cup dried red kidney beans, soaked

steps: Simmer the soaked beans with half the onion, 1 clove of garlic and water to cover for 50 minutes, until soft. Season with salt.
Cook the remaining onion, garlic and tomato in a little oil for 8 minutes for a hogao and stir half into the beans.
Pan-fry the pork belly slices in the oil for 12 minutes, until crisp and cooked through. Cook the chorizo in the same pan for 8 minutes.
Fry the plantain for 3 minutes per side, until golden, and the eggs until the whites are set.
Serve everything on a large plate with the rice and avocado.
notes: Food safety: pork must reach at least 70°C in the centre and rest before serving. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour. Cook the eggs until the whites are set. Kidney beans must be boiled hard for 10 minutes then simmered until fully soft.
Contains egg.

recipes.title: Pabellon Criollo (Venezuelan Shredded Beef, Black Beans and Plantain)
recipes.summary: Venezuela's national plate: slow-cooked shredded beef, black beans, rice and sweet fried plantain.
steps: Cover the beef with water, add the onion, garlic and 1 tsp salt and simmer for 2 hours, until it shreds easily. Cool slightly and shred.
Cook the capsicum and tomato in the olive oil for 8 minutes. Add the beef, cumin and 1/2 cup stock and simmer for 15 minutes, until saucy.
Warm the beans with the sugar and a splash of water for 8 minutes.
Fry the plantain in the vegetable oil for 3 minutes per side, until golden.
Serve the beef, beans and plantain in separate piles on a plate beside the rice.
notes: Food safety: beef is simmered well past 75°C in the centre until it shreds, and must be steaming hot when served. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour.
Dairy-free and gluten-free.

recipes.title: Seco de Cordero (Peruvian Lamb and Coriander Stew)
recipes.summary: Lamb braised in a vivid green coriander and beer sauce, served with rice and beans.
steps: Brown the lamb in the oil in a heavy pot for 8 minutes. Add the onion, garlic, cumin and aji paste and cook for 6 minutes.
Blend the coriander, spinach and beer into a smooth green paste. Pour into the pot with the stock.
Cover and simmer for 1 hour 15 minutes, until the lamb is tender. Add the potato for the last 25 minutes and the peas for the final 5.
Serve the stew in wide bowls beside the rice and spoon plenty of the green sauce over the top.
notes: Food safety: lamb pieces should reach at least 70°C and be tender. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour.
Dairy-free.
